sourceEvidence.quote:
Peripheral tolerance
Suppression/inactivation of self-reactive T/B cells (outside thymus/bone marrow) → preserves selftolerance; loss → autoimmunity.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.quote: Mechanisms: anergy, regulatory T-cell suppression, apoptosis (Fas–FasL pathway).

sourceEvidence.quote:
Anergy

kypExtensions.summary: Framing the two-signal rule as a safety interlock (signal 1 = the key, signal 2 = the license; key without license = anergy, not a weak response) and pairing it with the pharmacologic handles on the gate (CTLA-4-Ig blocking B7-CD28; checkpoint inhibitors releasing it) and the disease readouts (hyper-IgM at CD40L-CD40; ALPS at Fas-FasL).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source states the two-signal sequences and tolerance mechanisms but not the AND-gate framing, the drug-class connection, or the layer-failure disease map.
